name: Alex
label: Ambitious and anxious
headline: Alex, ambitious and anxious
summary: 21-ish, done with the 9-to-5 idea, learning to trade off free videos at 2am. Burned by a course or two and doesn't trust anyone selling one.

points.name: Trauma
points.sum: Grew up feeling average. The trades that went wrong took what confidence he had.
lines: Felt overlooked and average growing up; never “special.”
Frustrated with traditional education and life path (school → job → debt → stress).
Experienced loss of confidence from failed attempts at trading or investing.

points.name: Obstacles
points.sum: Nobody he trusts to show him the way, a family pushing the safe route, and a job eating his time.
lines: Lack of clear guidance in trading — overwhelmed by misinformation.
Trust issues due to past course scams and shady “gurus.”
Emotional rollercoaster of hope and doubt, causing inconsistent progress.
Pressure from family/friends to choose “stable” paths.
Difficulty balancing trading learning with work/school/family.

points.name: Age
points.sum: 19 to 24. Old enough to hate the 9-to-5, young enough to still be working out the way out.
lines: 19 to 24, early adulthood, at a crossroads in life.

points.name: Doubts
points.sum: Whether any of it is real, whether he's good enough, and whether he's about to waste money again.
lines: Am I good enough?
Are trading success stories real or scams?
Can I really escape the 9-to-5 grind?
Will I waste time and money again?

points.name: Goals
points.sum: $1k days, then $10k months. Enough to travel and take care of his family.
lines: Achieve financial freedom through trading.
Consistently make $1,000+ days, then $10k+ per month.
Build a lifestyle with freedom, travel, and luxury.
Support family financially without stress.

points.name: Fears
points.sum: Losing money, wasting more time on bad advice, and being stuck in a job forever.
lines: Fear of failure and losing money.
Fear of being stuck forever in a dead-end job.
Fear of wasting time on bad advice.
Fear of never truly trusting oneself or others again.

points.name: Insecurities
points.sum: Feels behind everyone his age, and he's starting to wonder if he's sharp or disciplined enough.
lines: Feeling “average” or “behind” peers who seem to be winning.
Lack of confidence after repeated failures.
Self-doubt about intelligence and discipline.

points.name: Vices
points.sum: Scrolls for motivation and ends up distracted. Picks up a new strategy every time the last one loses.
lines: Scrolling social media for motivation but getting distracted.
Chasing “shiny object syndrome” with new strategies or courses.
Occasional procrastination or avoidance when overwhelmed.

points.name: Thinks about
points.sum: How the guys his age pulled it off, and what his next move should be.
lines: How to break free financially.
How others made it and whether it’s possible for him.
What the next right step is.
Balancing hustle with mental health.

points.name: Beliefs
points.sum: Trading is real, most gurus aren't, and the right system would change everything.
lines: Trading is a legitimate path but requires real work.
Most “gurus” are scams, but some genuine help exists.
Financial freedom is achievable with the right system.

points.name: Identity
points.sum: Half regular guy, half entrepreneur. Wants it badly but hasn't fully committed yet.
lines: Split between “average guy” and “ambitious entrepreneur.”
Not fully committed yet but desperate to become successful.
Views himself as a learner, hustler, and hopeful dreamer.

points.name: Emotional patterns
points.sum: Hyped after a good video, flat after a loss. Quits, then comes straight back.
lines: High motivation spikes after inspiration.
Crippling self-doubt and anxiety cycles.
Frustration leading to quitting, then restarting.
Desire for control and certainty.

points.name: Resentments
points.sum: The normal path, the courses that took his money, and the people who don't get it.
lines: Resents societal pressure to follow traditional career paths.
Resents failed courses and wasted money.
Resents friends/family who don’t understand his goals.

points.name: Role models
points.sum: Young traders who are actually winning, and mentors with real results and no BS.
lines: Young successful traders and entrepreneurs on social media.
Mentors who show real results and no BS.

points.name: Media
points.sum: Trading YouTube, Instagram and TikTok, plus Discords and Whop groups.
lines: Instagram, TikTok, YouTube (trading content, motivational videos).
Trading forums and Discord groups & Whops

points.name: Platforms
points.sum: TradingView and Thinkorswim, and social media to learn and find his people.
lines: Trading apps (e.g., Thinkorswim, TradingView).
Social media for learning and community.

points.name: Routines
points.sum: Charts every day, late nights studying, journals for a week and then stops.
lines: Late nights researching and practicing trading.
Checking charts daily.
Scrolling social media for motivation and tactics.
Inconsistent journaling or habit tracking.

points.name: Family
points.sum: They want him in a stable job. He still wants to be the one who looks after them.
lines: Family expects “stable” career, causing friction.
Wants to support family financially.
Friends often don’t get or support his trading dreams.

points.name: Purchases
points.sum: Bought a course or two and some were a let-down. Still buys tools and books to get better.
lines: Bought 1-2 trading courses or mentorships, some disappointing.
Regularly invests in software, books, or tools to improve.

points.name: Wellbeing
points.sum: Stressed most of the time, and the late nights have wrecked his sleep.
lines: Mental stress from uncertainty and pressure.
Possible irregular sleep due to late-night trading research.

points.name: Traits
points.sum: Hungry and hardworking, but anxious, impatient and hard on himself.
lines: Ambitious, hardworking, and hungry.
Anxious, self-critical, and impatient.
Curious and open to learning but skeptical.

points.name: Values
points.sum: Freedom, real over hype, getting better, and his family.
lines: Freedom (time, financial, personal).
Authenticity — hates fake hype and BS.
Growth and self-improvement.
Responsibility toward family.

points.name: Education
points.sum: High school, maybe some college. Reckons school taught him nothing useful.
lines: Possibly some college or high school.
Feels traditional education didn’t prepare him for real life.

points.name: Social life
points.sum: Friends don't get it. His real crowd is the online trading groups.
lines: Limited understanding/support for trading from friends.
Online trading communities are his main “tribe.”

points.name: Hobbies
points.sum: Charts, motivational videos, probably some gaming.
lines: Trading and market analysis.
Watching motivational content.
Possibly gaming or social media.

points.name: Work experience
points.sum: Part-time or low-paid jobs to cover the bills. Maybe a side hustle or two.
lines: Part-time jobs or low-paying gigs to pay bills.
May have tried other side hustles.

points.name: Finances
points.sum: Not much spare cash, so any course he buys has to be worth it.
lines: Limited disposable income — cautious about spending on courses.
May have debt or financial pressure from family obligations.

pains.title: Every guru's a scam
pains.more: He's paid for courses that went nowhere, so every payout screenshot looks fake to him now.

pains.title: Got burned on a course
pains.more: The last one left him more confused, and money's tight. Getting it wrong twice would hurt.

pains.title: One red day and he's cooked
pains.more: A few green days and he thinks he's cracked it. One loss and he's asking if he's cut out for this.

pains.title: Everyone his age is winning
pains.more: His feed is people his age posting payouts and trips. It fires him up and stings at the same time.

pains.title: New strategy every week
pains.more: Free videos, PDFs, Discords. Plenty of info and no actual plan.

pains.title: Parents say get a real job
pains.more: They want him to be realistic. He wants to prove them wrong and still look after them.

feelings.name: Stress
feelings.meaning: Money, family pressure and late nights all pile on at once.

feelings.name: Fear
feelings.meaning: Losing money, and still being stuck in a job years from now.

feelings.name: Frustration
feelings.meaning: When it doesn't click he quits, then he's back the next week.

feelings.name: Shaky confidence
feelings.meaning: A few losses and he stops trusting his own calls.

feelings.name: Doubt
feelings.meaning: Whether any of this is real, and whether he's good enough.

feelings.name: Hope
feelings.meaning: He still believes the right system would change everything.

feelings.name: Anxiety
feelings.meaning: Self-doubt and anxiety come round in cycles.

feelings.name: Overwhelm
feelings.meaning: Too much information and no clear path through it.

brief: Alex has been burned by courses and gurus, so he doesn't trust anyone selling one. What gets through to him is a trader he can watch for real, one clear method taught step by step, and steady progress over flashy cars or big numbers. He wants real talk, no hype.

needs.struggle: Trust issues due to past course scams and shady gurus
needs.need: A trader he can watch before he pays
needs.hear: I'll show you my trades, the losing ones too, before I ever ask you to join anything.
needs.see: Real trades taken live, with the losses left in.

make.title: watch me trade live, losses included (step by step)

make.idea: Show a losing trade and how you handled it. No highlight reel.

needs.struggle: Will I waste time and money again?
needs.need: To know exactly what he gets before he buys
needs.hear: Here's exactly what happens in your first week with me, and what it won't do for you.
needs.see: The inside of the mentorship, from day one to the first review.

make.idea: Walk through your mentorship like a tour and answer the 'what if it's another dud' question.
What he gets with you that a course never gave him.

needs.struggle: Loss of confidence from failed attempts at trading or investing
needs.hear: Every trader has losing streaks. Here's what I do the morning after one.
needs.see: A trader handling a red day calmly, step by step.

make.title: how to trade again after a losing streak (step by step)

make.idea: Film the morning after a red day and say what you do next. Phone in hand, no edit.

needs.struggle: Feeling average or behind peers who seem to be winning
needs.need: Proof someone like him made it
needs.hear: Most of what you see online is a highlight reel. Here's where I was at your age.
needs.see: Where the trader was at 21, next to where he is now.

make.title: how i went from [your real number] to [your real number] a month trading

make.idea: Where you were at his age and the one thing that actually changed.
Your day now next to your day back then. No flexing.

needs.struggle: Chasing shiny object syndrome with new strategies or courses
needs.need: One method he can stick to
needs.hear: Jumping to a new setup after every loss is what keeps you stuck.
needs.see: One method broken into steps, and what sticking to it looks like over a month.

make.title: the one setup i'd trade if i started again (step by step)

make.idea: Why jumping setups after every loss keeps you stuck.

needs.struggle: Pressure from family and friends to choose stable paths
needs.need: Proof this is a real path
needs.hear: Your family wants you safe. Show them a plan with rules and limits, and they'll come round.
needs.see: A trader with a routine, rules and risk limits, run like a real job.

make.idea: If your family doubted you too, tell that story and where it stands now.
What you'd say to his parents about trading, straight up.
